skill.name: xlsx
skill.description: Create, edit, analyze, and validate Excel spreadsheets with formulas, formatting, data workflows, and optional LibreOffice recalculation.
skill.summary: Guides spreadsheet creation, analysis, formatting, formula validation, and recalculation for XLSX workflows.
skill.author: ArtemisAI

security_audit.summary: Most SKILL.md detections are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline spreadsheet examples. The recalc.py helper has real risk because it runs LibreOffice and installs a persistent macro in the user profile. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Store automation in a temporary isolated LibreOffice profile or require explicit user consent before writing Module1.xba into the default profile.

remediation.issue: External LibreOffice execution on user-provided files
remediation.suggestion: Run soffice with a restricted profile, document the external command clearly, and avoid processing untrusted workbooks unless the user approves.
Add row, column, file size, and timeout limits before scanning all workbook cells for formulas and errors.

finding_verdicts.reason: The script starts the local soffice binary to initialize LibreOffice state. Arguments are hardcoded and no shell is used, but launching an external office process is a real execution and profile-modification risk.
This is a hardcoded gtimeout --version availability check with no shell and no user-controlled arguments. It does not create a command injection path.

The script runs LibreOffice headlessly against a caller-provided workbook path and invokes an application macro. There is no shell interpolation, but processing untrusted spreadsheets through an external office suite is a meaningful execution risk.
The detected URL is an OpenOffice XML namespace inside a macro document. It is not used for an HTTP request or network communication.
The code targets the hidden LibreOffice profile directory under the user home directory. This is persistent application configuration outside the current workspace.
The script reads and writes under ~/.config/libreoffice or the macOS LibreOffice profile. This hidden profile access is intentional but security-relevant because it persists beyond one run.
The script writes Module1.xba into the LibreOffice macro directory. That creates or replaces executable office macro content in a persistent user profile location.
The script creates the LibreOffice macro directory under the user profile when it is missing. This is a persistent filesystem modification outside the workbook being processed.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent LibreOffice Macro Installation
semantic_findings.description: The recalculation helper automatically creates a LibreOffice Basic macro named RecalculateAndSave in the user profile and reuses it on later runs. This persists executable office automation outside the current workbook or project directory.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code builds a Module1.xba macro under the LibreOffice profile and writes it when missing. The behavior is direct and intentional.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Workbook Cell Scanning
semantic_findings.description: The recalculation helper scans every row and cell in each workbook twice without size limits. A very large workbook can cause excessive CPU or memory use during validation.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code explicitly iterates through all rows and cells for values and formulas. Legitimate use is possible, but there are no safeguards for oversized inputs.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often needs formulas, formatting, and validation across Excel files. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through XLSX creation, editing, analysis, and recalculation.
actual_capabilities: Reads and analyzes Excel, CSV, and TSV data with pandas workflows.
Creates and edits XLSX workbooks with formulas, sheets, formatting, and cell styles.
Preserves existing workbook templates when modifying spreadsheet files.
Recalculates formulas through a bundled LibreOffice helper script.
Checks recalculated workbooks for common Excel formula errors.
Applies financial model formatting conventions for inputs, formulas, links, and assumptions.
limitations: Formula recalculation requires LibreOffice to be installed and available as soffice.
The helper script writes a LibreOffice macro into the user profile unless changed by the author.
openpyxl can preserve formulas, but it cannot calculate formula results by itself.
Very large workbooks may need scoped reading to avoid slow analysis.

use_cases.title: Build Financial Models
use_cases.description: Create projection workbooks with formulas, assumption cells, source notes, and standard finance formatting.

use_cases.title: Clean Operational Reports
use_cases.description: Read raw spreadsheets, normalize columns, create summary tabs, and export a usable XLSX report.

use_cases.title: Validate Formula Workbooks
use_cases.description: Recalculate formulas, find spreadsheet errors, and identify cells that need correction before delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Workbook
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new spreadsheet.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an XLSX workbook for monthly expenses with categories, totals, and simple formatting. Use formulas for all totals.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Spreadsheet Data
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this spreadsheet, summarize the key trends, and create a clean Excel output with a summary sheet and charts.

prompt_templates.title: Update an Existing Template
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for preserving workbook style.
prompt_templates.prompt: Update this existing workbook with the new data while preserving its formulas, formatting, sheet names, and layout conventions.

prompt_templates.title: Validate a Formula Model
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for recalculation and error review.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this XLSX financial model, recalculate formulas, report any formula errors, and fix references while preserving the template.

output_examples.input: Create a revenue tracker with monthly totals and year-to-date calculations.
output_examples.output: A formatted workbook with monthly revenue rows, formula-driven totals, year-to-date calculations, and clear input cells.

output_examples.input: Analyze a sales spreadsheet and prepare a management summary.
output_examples.output: A cleaned Excel file with a summary worksheet, key metrics, trend notes, and source data preserved in separate sheets.

output_examples.input: Check this workbook for formula errors after editing.
output_examples.output: A validation summary listing error types, affected cells, total formulas checked, and recommended corrections.

best_practices: Use spreadsheet formulas for calculated workbook values instead of hardcoding Python results.
Preserve existing workbook formatting and template conventions when editing files.
Recalculate and validate formula workbooks before delivering final XLSX files.
anti_patterns: Do not save a workbook opened with data_only=True when formulas must be preserved.
Do not hardcode calculated totals, ratios, or growth rates into output cells.
Do not process very large workbooks without scoping sheets, columns, or rows.

faq.question: Can this skill create new Excel files?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides workflows for creating XLSX workbooks with sheets, formulas, formatting, and workbook structure.

faq.question: Can it edit existing spreadsheets?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends preserving existing formulas, formatting, sheet names, and template conventions during edits.

faq.question: Does it calculate Excel formulas directly?
faq.answer: The Python libraries preserve formulas but do not calculate results. The bundled helper uses LibreOffice for recalculation.

faq.question: Does the skill need external software?
faq.answer: Yes. Formula recalculation depends on LibreOffice and the local soffice command being available.

faq.question: Can it work with CSV and TSV files?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance includes pandas workflows for reading, analyzing, and exporting spreadsheet-like data.

faq.question: Is it suitable for financial models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes conventions for assumptions, source notes, formula construction, number formats, and finance color coding.
